items.title: Stefon Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2020
items.q: I see a photo of Duke Ellington or whoever it is in my room and they remind me of the importance of staying focused on why art is important.

ctx.x: You know every single day, from where I’m sitting at the piano or on the vibes, I’m writing and creating. I see a photo of Duke Ellington or whoever it is in my room and they remind me of the importance of staying focused on why art is important. Art is not important in our society because of the individual talent of an artist or an individual artist’s ego. Art is important because it’s a reflection of what’s happening in the world right now. The reason that Herbie Hancock back there and Miles Davis, all these…

I’m glad you said that, because it seems there is so much to reflect in the arts now, maybe just so many things that are happening all at the same time, yet over my shoulder are Lester Young and Count Basie, and incredible to think that their music at the time was probably eighty years ago. And do you feel that what they were doing carried as much significance to the community as what you are doing?
